causes.explanation: The traceback shows line.amount is a str when it reaches format_money, which points to how Line computes amount from product.price. Because the price is a str from c1, arithmetic like price * qty yields a str (repetition), not a number.
causes.fix_hint: Ensure Line.amount is computed from a numeric price, which requires fixing the price type at load time.

causes.title: format_money trusts untyped input without validation
causes.explanation: format_money is annotated amount: float but performs no runtime check, so a str fails only at the format spec. Adding a conversion or type guard here would surface the bad value closer to its source, though it would hide rather than fix the upstream cause.
causes.fix_hint: Add a float() conversion or isinstance check at the top of format_money to fail early with a clearer message.

causes.title: load_catalog leaves price as raw CSV string
causes.explanation: In load_catalog, price=row["price"] is never converted to float, while stock and weight_kg are cast. Product.price therefore holds a str, so Line.amount becomes str * int or str, and format_money receives a string.

causes.title: Line.amount multiplies str price by qty
causes.explanation: Line.amount computes self.product.price * self.qty, which yields a string (repeated) when price is a str, so the bad type propagates into format_money. This is where the wrong value surfaces, not where it originates.
causes.fix_hint: Ensure Product.price is numeric before arithmetic, rather than coercing inside amount.

causes.title: format_money called with non-numeric amount
causes.explanation: format_money assumes a float but receives a str from Line.amount. Its contract is not enforced, so the crash occurs at the format spec instead of at the conversion point.
causes.fix_hint: Coerce the amount to float in format_money or fix the upstream price type.

error_line: IndexError: list index out of range

causes.title: _rank_index rounds to n, producing an out-of-range index
causes.explanation: For p/100*n rounding up to n, the index equals len(ordered), which is invalid. For example, p=99 with n=1 gives round(0.99)=1, and p=90 with n=2 gives round(1.8)=2. The index should be bounded by n-1.
causes.fix_hint: Compute the index from (n-1) and clamp it to the range [0, n-1].

causes.title: per_route passes tiny route groups to percentile
causes.explanation: Routes with only one or two records make p90 or p99 hit the bad index. percentile only guards against empty input, so single-element and two-element lists still reach the faulty rank calculation.
causes.fix_hint: Guard percentile for small sample sizes or fix the rank calculation so it cannot reach len.

causes.title: API filter leaves many single-record routes in the data
causes.explanation: only_api keeps every /api/ route regardless of how many requests it has, so sparse routes survive into per_route. This upstream data shape is what exposes the small-sample overflow.
causes.fix_hint: Drop or merge routes below a minimum request count before computing percentiles.

causes.title: Empty times list passed to percentile for a route
causes.explanation: per_route builds times from records in each group, but percentile's early return only guards empty lists, and _rank_index(n, 99) with n=1 or small n can yield index equal to n when p/100*n rounds up past the end. For p=100-ish rounding the index can reach len(ordered), so an out-of-range index is produced from the percentile math itself rather than from empty data.
causes.fix_hint: Clamp the rank index to len(ordered)-1 inside _rank_index or percentile.

causes.title: Rank index formula can exceed list bounds
causes.explanation: _rank_index uses int(round(p / 100 * n)) with no clamping, so for p=99 and small n the rounded value can equal n, which is out of range for ordered[...]. The crash at line 31 is the first place this bad index is used.
causes.fix_hint: Use a clamped nearest-rank formula such as min(n - 1, max(0, round(p / 100 * n) - 1)).

causes.title: Unfiltered api list passed to per_route
causes.explanation: build_report feeds per_route the result of filters.clean(filters.only_api(records)), so routes can end up with very few or unusual timing values. Upstream filtering that produces a sparse group makes the percentile computation more fragile.
causes.fix_hint: Guard per_route or percentile so that groups with no valid timings return 0.0 instead of indexing.

causes.title: Parser admits lines with zero response time
causes.explanation: parse_line accepts any digit sequence for ms, so zero or absent timing values can flow into latency lists; this is where a degenerate input is created, though the crash occurs later in percentile.
causes.fix_hint: Validate that ms is present and positive in the parsed record before it reaches stats.

error_line: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'route'

causes.title: parse_line returns None for some log lines
causes.explanation: load_records keeps every parse_line result without filtering, so any line the parser rejects becomes a None entry in records. The first attribute access on that entry, r.route in only_api, is where it crashes.
causes.fix_hint: Make parse_line raise or skip malformed lines, and filter out None results in load_records before returning.

causes.title: load_records passes unfiltered parse results downstream
causes.explanation: load_records returns the raw list from parse_line without a None check, so the bad value leaks into every consumer of records. only_api is the first consumer to dereference it.
causes.fix_hint: Filter out None values before returning the records list from load_records.

causes.title: build_report filters by route before cleaning
causes.explanation: build_report calls only_api on the raw records before clean, so no None check runs first. Filtering or guarding None earlier in the pipeline would stop the crash at this call.
causes.fix_hint: Drop None records right after loading so that only_api and clean never see them.

causes.title: only_api lacks a guard for None records
causes.explanation: only_api accesses r.route on every element without checking for None. This is the crash site, though the underlying bad value comes from earlier in the pipeline.
causes.fix_hint: Skip None entries in the comprehension, for example with a 'r is not None and' guard.

causes.title: parse_line returns None for blank or comment lines
causes.explanation: parse_line returns None for empty or '#' lines, and load_records keeps those None values in the list without filtering them. Those None entries then reach only_api, where r.route is accessed on None.
causes.fix_hint: Filter out None values in load_records, e.g. skip falsy results from parse_line before returning.

causes.title: load_records does not filter None results from parse_line
causes.explanation: The list comprehension in load_records stores every parse_line result, including None, so the None values are created here and propagate to the caller. This is the point where the bad value enters the pipeline.
causes.fix_hint: Change the return to filter out None, such as records = [r for r in (parse_line(l) for l in lines) if r is not None].

causes.title: main passes unfiltered records into build_report
causes.explanation: main calls load_records and passes its result directly to build_report without removing None entries, so the bad list is handed downstream unchecked.
causes.fix_hint: Validate or filter the records list in main before calling build_report.

error_line: ValueError: time data '25/Oct/2026:09:00:00 -0700' does not match format '%d/%m/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z'

causes.title: TIME_FORMAT uses numeric month but logs use abbreviated month
causes.explanation: The log timestamp '25/Oct/2026' contains the abbreviated month name 'Oct', but TIME_FORMAT expects a numeric month via %m. The format string was written for a different timestamp style than the Apache-style logs being parsed.
causes.fix_hint: Change TIME_FORMAT to use %b instead of %m, i.e. "%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z".

causes.title: LINE_RE captures a time format the parser does not expect
causes.explanation: The regex group for time accepts any non-bracket text, so it passes through the Apache-style timestamp without validating it against TIME_FORMAT. The mismatch is only detected later, inside parse_time.
causes.fix_hint: Make the time capture in LINE_RE match the actual log timestamp layout, or validate it when parsing the line.

causes.title: Log file contains timestamps in a different format
causes.explanation: The input file may have been generated with a timestamp style (month names) that differs from what the parser was written for. The parser code is consistent with itself, so the mismatch likely originates in the data source.
causes.fix_hint: Confirm the log producer's timestamp format and align the parser with it.

causes.title: TIME_FORMAT uses numeric %m but log has month names
causes.explanation: The format expects a numeric month (%m), but the log timestamp '25/Oct/2026' uses an abbreviated month name, which requires %b. The constant was written for a different timestamp style than this log uses.
causes.fix_hint: Change TIME_FORMAT to "%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z" so the abbreviated month name parses.

causes.title: Log data uses a different timestamp format than assumed
causes.explanation: The access log was written in the common Apache/nginx style with month abbreviations, but the parser was built for numeric months. The mismatch is in the input data's format, not in the parsing logic itself.
causes.fix_hint: Confirm the log's time format and either normalize the input or make the parser accept both numeric and named months.

causes.title: LINE_RE accepts any text in the time group
causes.explanation: The regex captures everything between brackets without checking that it looks like a valid timestamp. Malformed or differently formatted times pass through to strptime unvalidated and fail there.
causes.fix_hint: Tighten the time group in LINE_RE to match the expected timestamp shape so bad values are caught earlier.

causes.title: parse_line errors are not caught; one bad line aborts load
causes.explanation: load_records has no error handling, so a single unparseable timestamp raises and stops the whole run. This turns a per-line format problem into a full crash.
causes.fix_hint: Catch ValueError per line in load_records, log or skip the bad record, and continue.

causes.title: Depth uses 0-based roots, inconsistent with row sizing

causes.fix_hint: Either keep 0-based depths and size rows as max+1, or switch to 1-based depths and index rows accordingly.

causes.explanation: plan() calls levels with the same order used for earliest_times, so the input is valid. This candidate is unlikely because the failure is independent of the order contents.

causes.title: Stage list sized one short of the deepest level
causes.explanation: Depth values start at 0 for root tasks (default=-1 plus 1), so the deepest level equals max(depth) and is an invalid index into rows, which has max(depth) entries. Any non-empty project triggers this crash.
causes.fix_hint: Size rows as max(depth.values()) + 1 so that index max(depth) exists.

causes.title: Depth numbering starts at zero, not one
causes.explanation: The depth formula uses default=-1, so root tasks get depth 0 and the stage numbering is zero-based while the row count is derived as if depths were one-based. This mismatch between depth creation and row allocation is the origin of the bad index.
causes.fix_hint: Either make root depth 1 (default=0) or allocate max(depth)+1 rows so depth is used as a zero-based index.

causes.title: Levels computed over an order that may be incomplete
causes.explanation: If order omitted some task ids, depth would lack entries, but the crash shows a valid key lookup, so this is unlikely to be the cause. It is listed only as a secondary check on the order passed in from plan().

causes.title: Project.get lowercases ids but stored keys are uppercase

causes.title: No None guard after project.get in earliest_times
causes.explanation: earliest_times assumes project.get always returns a Task and dereferences task.deps immediately. A missing lookup therefore crashes here instead of surfacing a clear lookup error.

causes.title: topo_order passes uppercase keys into case-sensitive get
